# LOCK T: FSOT-picked topology. Selection rule, analytic screen and blind predictions, locked BEFORE simulating any candidate

## Fixed FSOT value
The damping is A = γ_rel = 0.42804344605980688 (fsot-law-circuit DESIGN.md:33, results/design.json:3). It is not tuned.

## Candidates (16; all listed in topo/screen.json, generated by topo/screen.py)
- **F1 (7 candidates):** the |x| jerk x''' + γ_rel x'' + B x' = |x| − 1, with B taken from every applied FSOT ratio {1, K, Θ, κ, κ/γ_rel, γ_rel, S_EM}.
  - Theorem (time and amplitude rescaling): this family depends only on A_eff = A/√B, whatever the slope and offset of the nonlinearity.
  - A_eff = 0.428, 0.660, 0.447, 0.763, 0.499, 0.654, 0.438. **None** lies in the known canonical chaos bands, [0.547, 0.6405] ideal and [0.529, 0.584] with the real diode. All 7 fail analytically.
- **F2 (9 candidates):** unit-coefficient one-nonlinearity jerks x''' + γ_rel x'' + B x' + C x = ±N(x) + E, with N ∈ {sgn (comparator), |x| (diode)} and B, C ∈ {0, 1}. Labels S-a … S-f and A-a … A-c.

## Analytic chaos screen (necessary conditions; computed, not simulated)
A candidate passes if:
- (i) it has at least 2 equilibria;
- (ii) every equilibrium is unstable;
- (iii) every equilibrium is a saddle-focus satisfying the Shilnikov inequality |Re λ_c| / |λ_r| < 1;
- (iv) it is dissipative (div = −γ_rel < 0).

Passers: S-a, S-c, A-a, A-b, A-c.

## Selection rule
The winner is the screen-passer with the **fewest parts**, counted as op-amps + diodes + resistors + capacitors, with ties broken by fewer op-amps.
**Winner: S-a, x''' = −γ_rel x'' − x + sgn(x).** Parts: 4 op-amps (3 integrators + 1 comparator; one TL074), 0 diodes, 5 resistors, 3 capacitors.
- Equilibria x* = ±1, eigenvalues −1.16493 and 0.36844 ± 0.85010i, Shilnikov ratio 0.3163.
- The system is homogeneous: x → c·x with sgn amplitude c. So the comparator swing and the input resistor only set the volt scale, and the dynamics depend on γ_rel alone. **No knob.**

All 16 candidates are then simulated (C++20 engine topo/tj.cpp) for transparency. The selection does not depend on those runs.

## Blind predictions for the winner S-a (A = γ_rel; τ0 = 1.8 kΩ · 100 nF = 180 µs)
| ID | prediction | pass band |
|---|---|---|
| T1 | chaotic: λ1 > 0.005/τ0, bounded, in ≥ 3 of 4 initial conditions (C++ ideal) | as stated |
| T2 | λ1 + λ2 + λ3 = −γ_rel = −0.42804 | |sum + 0.42804| < 0.005 |
| T3 | dominant frequency ≈ Im λ_c / (2π τ0) = 0.85010/(2π·180 µs) = **751.7 Hz** | ±15 % |
| T4 | ngspice (TI TL082 model, comparator from one TL07x section, R_A = R/γ_rel = 4205 Ω → E96 4.22 kΩ) is chaotic (> 40 distinct maxima of V(x)) | as stated |
| T5 | the attractor is symmetric under x → −x (or a symmetric pair) because the system is odd: |mean(x)| < 0.1·max|x| over 4 ICs (C++) | as stated |
